t: A particle retards from a velocity v₀ while moving in a straight line. If the magnitude of deceleration is directly proportional to the square root of the speed of the particle, find its average velocity for the total time of its motion.
s:
Let the acceleration of the particle be a=−k√v, where k is a positive constant and v is the velocity.
To find the total time T taken to come to rest, using a=dv/dt:
dv/dt=−k√v
∫_v₀^0 v^(−1/2)dv=−k∫_0^T dt
[2v^(1/2)]_(v₀)⁰=−kT
−2√v₀=−kT⇒T=2√v₀/k
To find the total distance S covered before coming to rest, using a=vdv/dx:
vdv/dx=−k√v
√vdv=−kdx
∫_v₀^0 v^(1/2)dv=−k∫_0^S dx
[2/3v^(3/2)]_(v₀)⁰=−kS
−2/3v₀^(3/2)=−kS⇒S=(2v₀^(3/2))/3k
The average velocity is the total distance divided by the total time:
v_(avg)=S/T=((2v₀^(3/2))/3k)/(2√v₀/k)
v_(avg)=(v₀^(3/2))/3√v₀=v₀/3 .

The relative velocity of each taxi with reference to a taxi coming from the other side.
